object_types.name: Reviewer
object_types.definition: A person who reviews papers for the conference

source_references.excerpt: Reviewers review papers. A reviewer can review many papers, and each paper gets several reviewers
Reviewers have a reviewer ID.

object_types.name: Paper
object_types.definition: A submitted paper being reviewed for the conference

source_references.excerpt: Reviewers review papers. A reviewer can review many papers, and each paper gets several reviewers
Papers have a paper number.

object_types.name: Review
object_types.definition: The act of a particular reviewer reviewing a particular paper, treated as an object in its own right, identified by a review ID

source_references.excerpt: And each completed review gets its own review ID -- we treat the review itself as a thing we track.
The review is the act of a particular reviewer reviewing a particular paper -- the score hangs off that pairing, not off the paper alone.

object_types.name: Review Score
object_types.definition: The overall rating given in a review

source_references.excerpt: Every review has exactly one review score -- that is our term for the overall rating. The review score is always one of 1, 2, 3, 4, or 5.
Reviewers review papers. A reviewer can review many papers, and each paper gets several reviewers, but a given reviewer reviews a given paper at most once.

fact_types.name: Review has Review Score
readings: Review Score is the score of Review

source_references.excerpt: Every review has exactly one review score -- that is our term for the overall rating.
A review without a score is not a review -- it always has exactly one.
